name: Preparing for your new kitchen flooring installation: A quick guide

step.name: Step 1: Clear the Space — Before the installation team arrives, it's crucial to completely empty your kitchen. This means clearing out all dishes, food, small appliances, and anything on the countertops. You'll also need to disconnect and move larger appliances like your refrigerator, stove, and dishwasher. This typically takes a few hours to a day, depending on how much stuff you have, and makes the installer's job much quicker.

This typically takes a few hours to a day, depending on how much stuff you have, and makes the installer's job much quicker.

step.name: Step 2: Protect Adjacent Areas — To prevent dust and debris from spreading throughout your home, cover doorways with plastic sheeting and protect furniture in adjacent rooms. Lay down drop cloths or old blankets in high-traffic areas leading to the kitchen. This step is important for keeping your home cleaner during what can be a dusty process and takes about an hour or two.

step.name: Step 3: Subfloor Readiness — The success of your new flooring largely depends on a properly prepared subfloor. If old flooring needs to be removed, that will be done first. Then, the subfloor needs to be clean, dry, level, and free of any damage. Any unevenness or defects in the subfloor can cause issues with your new flooring down the line, such as squeaks or cracks. This is a critical step that our team at Simply Construction handles, and it can take anywhere from a few hours to a full day, depending on the condition of your existing subfloor.

step.name: Step 4: Appliance Storage and Access — Plan where large appliances will go during the installation. If they can’t stay in an adjacent room, consider a garage or storage unit. Also, ensure there’s a clear path for installers to bring in materials and tools. Making sure this is clear before they arrive can save a lot of time and hassle on installation day.
